entities.summary:
Lupo di Francesco was an Italian sculptor and architect, active in Pisa.

Born into a family of artists, Lupo di Francesco honed his skills in the city's prestigious workshop of Michelangelo Buonarroti.

Between 1375 and 1400, Lupo di Francesco designed and constructed several prominent buildings, including the Pisa Cathedral's facade, which showcased his innovative use of terracotta and brick.

His work had a lasting impact on the city's architectural style, influencing generations of builders and architects.

As a testament to his skill, Lupo di Francesco's masterpiece, the Pisa Cathedral's facade, remains an iconic symbol of Italian Renaissance architecture.

A striking example of his craftsmanship, the cathedral's facade features intricate carvings and ornate details that have withstood the test of time.

The legacy of Lupo di Francesco can be seen in the many buildings and monuments he designed, which continue to inspire artists and architects today.

In 1400, Lupo di Francesco passed away, leaving behind a body of work that would be remembered for centuries to come.
